title: Creating a React App with Vite
summary: A React project needs tools that prepare its code for the browser. Vite is one tool that can do this.
introduction: A React project needs tools that prepare its code for the browser. Vite is one tool that can do this. Create a small project with help if you need it. Start the local preview, open the page and change one greeting.
learningObjectives: Create a React project from the Vite template with one command
Explain the role of index.html, main.jsx and App.jsx
Run the development server and use hot module replacement
Produce and preview a production build

blocks.text: For years the standard starter was Create React App. It was deprecated in early 2025, and the React documentation now points client-side projects to **Vite** (or to a full framework such as Next.js when you need server rendering). Vite serves your source files as native ES modules during development, so the server starts in milliseconds and edits show up almost instantly; for production it bundles everything into a handful of optimized files.
You need Node.js. Vite 7 requires Node 20.19 or newer (or 22.12 or newer on the 22 line), so install a current LTS release from nodejs.org and check it in a terminal:

blocks.code:
npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react
cd my-react-app
npm install
npm run dev

blocks.text: The first command downloads the `create-vite` package and generates a folder. The `--` matters: it separates npm's own options from the ones meant for `create-vite`; without it `--template` is swallowed by npm and you land in the interactive prompt instead. Use `--template react-ts` if you want TypeScript. The last command starts the development server:

blocks.title: npm run dev (version and timing vary)
blocks.content:
VITE v7.1.5  ready in 312 ms

  ➜  Local:   http://localhost:5173/
  ➜  Network: use --host to expose
  ➜  press h + enter to show help

blocks.text: Open `http://localhost:5173` and you see the template's demo page with a counter button. Keep the terminal open; the server keeps running until you press Ctrl+C.

blocks.title: Project structure
blocks.code:
my-react-app/
├── index.html          # the only HTML page
├── package.json
├── vite.config.js      # Vite configuration with the React plugin
├── eslint.config.js
├── public/             # static files copied as-is
└── src/
    ├── main.jsx        # entry point: mounts <App /> into #root
    ├── App.jsx         # the demo component
    ├── App.css
    ├── index.css
    └── assets/

blocks.title: src/main.jsx

blocks.text: `createRoot` from `react-dom/client` is how React 18 and 19 attach to a DOM element; the older `ReactDOM.render` was removed in React 19. `StrictMode` is a development-only wrapper that renders each component twice and runs effects twice to surface impure code and missing cleanups. It changes nothing in a production build.
Delete the generated `App.css` import and the demo markup and start with something small:

blocks.title: src/App.jsx

blocks.text: Save the file and look at the browser: the page updates without a reload. That is **hot module replacement** (HMR), and the React plugin's Fast Refresh keeps component state across edits whenever it can, so you can tweak the markup of a form without retyping what you had entered into it.

blocks.code:
npm run build
npm run preview

blocks.title: npm run build (hashes, sizes and timing vary)
blocks.content:
vite v7.1.5 building for production...

dist/assets/index-BxQ3k2Lm.css    1.39 kB │ gzip:  0.72 kB

blocks.text: `build` writes a `dist/` folder with minified JavaScript and CSS whose file names contain content hashes for cache busting. That folder is a static site: upload it to any static host. `preview` serves it locally so you can check the real build rather than the dev server.

blocks.title: Common mistake: opening index.html as a file
blocks.text: Double-clicking `index.html` or `dist/index.html` opens it with a `file://` URL, and the page stays blank: module scripts and absolute asset paths need an HTTP server. During development use `npm run dev`; to check a build use `npm run preview` or any static file server.

blocks.title: Install React DevTools
blocks.text: The React Developer Tools extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox adds a Components tab that shows the component tree with its props and state, and a Profiler tab that the performance lesson uses. Install it now; you will reach for it in every lesson.

questions.question: Which file creates the React root and renders `<App />`?
questions.explanation: `src/main.jsx` calls `createRoot(document.getElementById('root')).render(<App />)`. `index.html` only provides the empty `#root` element.

questions.question: `StrictMode` slows down the production build because it renders every component twice.
questions.explanation: Strict Mode's double rendering and double effects happen only in development. In a production build it has no effect at all.
